title: Open-closed short exact sequence on the pro-etale site
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ the inclusion of the complementary open subscheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and assume that $j$ is quasi-compact. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] let $i^*,j^*$ be the inverse images and $i_*$ the direct image of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], and $j_!$ the extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Then for every sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $\Lambda_X$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ the sequence
$$
0\longrightarrow j_!j^*\mathcal F\longrightarrow\mathcal F\longrightarrow i_*i^*\mathcal F\longrightarrow0,
$$
whose first map is the counit of $j_!\dashv j^*$ and whose second map is the unit of $i^*\dashv i_*$, is exact.

proof.text: Use the existing module-valued closed-counit theorem [lem-exc-proetale-closed-fully-faithful], namely AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isIso_upperStarLowerStarAdjunction_counit from WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.ProEtale.UpperLowerStar.ClosedImmersion. No new affine, mate, continuity, or localization theorem is stated or proved here.

In the same existing source-library module, isZero_upperStar_lowerStar_of_disjoint shows that open restriction of closed direct image vanishes. The range-complement hypothesis supplies its disjointness hypothesis. By the two adjunctions, closed restriction of extension by zero also vanishes, and the counit-unit composite is zero. The existing isIso_of_isIso_upperStar_of_isCompl from that module gives joint detection for the complementary restrictions; package it as JointlyReflectIsomorphisms for their pair functor. This reuses the already proved section-detection argument without copying it.

Apply JointlyReflectIsomorphisms.shortExact_iff to the short complex with the specified counit and unit. Closed restriction has zero first term and invertible second arrow, by the closed counit and the left triangle identity. Open restriction has invertible first arrow and zero third term, by full faithfulness of extension by zero and the right triangle identity. ShortComplex.exact_iff_mono and exact_iff_epi prove exactness of these two restrictions. Thus the original complex is short exact; project its monomorphism, epimorphism and composable-arrows exactness fields.

theorem exact_openClosedSequence (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ]
    {X Z U : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) (j : U ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsOpenImmersion j] [QuasiCompact j]
    (hU : Set.range j = (Set.range i)ᶜ)
    (F : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) :
    Mono ((openImmersionLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j).counit.app F) ∧
      Epi ((upperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) i).unit.app F) ∧
      (ComposableArrows.mk₂
        ((openImmersionLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j).counit.app F)
        ((upperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) i).unit.app F)).Exact
